newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG FACES TOUGH TEST ON RIVAL'S HOME SNOW.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG FACES TOUGH TEST ON RIVAL'S HOME SNOW.

text.p: Pernilla Wiberg, a softly-spoken Swede who skis with the nerve of a lion, will need all her composure when she takes on rival Katja Seizinger on the German's home snow this weekend.

The women's Alpine skiing World Cup circuit returns to Zwiesel for the first time for six years with two giant slaloms and a slalom on the programme for Friday, Saturday and Sunday, the start of an intensive two weeks.

Double world champion and overall World Cup leader Wiberg was a powerful force in giant slalom in the early part of her career, winning gold medals at the 1991 world championships and 1992 Albertville Olympics.
But the Swede has struggled in the discipline in recent seasons and has won only one World Cup giant slalom during her career -- back in 1991.
Her 214-point lead over title holder Seizinger in the overall rankings could be eroded in Zwiesel. The German is joint leader of the giant slalom standings with Italian Sabina Panzanini.
"My goal is to get on the podium again in a giant slalom," said Wiberg who used to be a technical specialist but is now turning rapidly into an all-rounder.
Wiberg was a picture of composure last weekend during three days of chaotic weather in the Austrian resort of Bad Kleinkirchheim when she recorded her fourth World Cup of the season in a super-G.
The Swede has set her sights this season on her first overall World Cup triumph.

As world slalom champion, Wiberg is the favourite for Sunday's race. But she will need to improve her giant slalom form in Zwiesel and in the Italian resort of Cortina d'Ampezzo next week to keep up her challenge in the overall rankings.
Italian Deborah Compagnoni, who is fourth in the overall World Cup standings and the reigning world giant slalom champion, is also expected to make a strong bid to improve her overall position.

This could also be the weekend when Germany's Martina Ertl, a bronze medallist in the giant slalom at last year's world championships, boosts her position in the overall standings after injury problems earlier in the season.
